data.content_ref: inline:The target's refusal condition is over-stated as a necessary condition. It claims resumption 'must be refused if framing lacks such delimiters,' treating self-delimiting records with end-markers and checksums as the sole covering principle for safe resumption. But append-only identity is preserved by not modifying or deleting committed events—a condition that can be satisfied without self-delimiting framing. A protocol could maintain an external verified-offset manifest (e.g., a separate commit-log or checkpoint pointer) recording the byte position of the last complete event, allowing the resumption process to skip the trailing partial fragment without interpreting or modifying it. The partial bytes remain physically in the append-only log untouched, and new events are appended after them (or after a separator marker). This preserves append-only identity of recorded events even though the framing itself lacks end-markers or checksums. The target thus fails the problem's demand to 'adjudicate between rival criteria' because it collapses the design space into a single criterion and misclassifies an externally-checkpointed but non-self-delimiting protocol as necessarily refused, when the append-only invariant could still hold.
